Text 1 is adapted from E.M. Forster’s 1910 novel Howards End. Text 2 discusses Howards
End. King’s Cross and St. Pancras are adjacent railway terminals in London from which
trains travel to the countryside.

Text1

To Margaret the station of King’s Cross had always suggested Infinity. Its very situation—
withdrawn a little behind the facile splendours of St. Pancras—implied a comment on the
materialism of life. Those two great arches, colourless, indifferent, shouldering between
them an unlovely clock, were fit portals for some eternal adventure, whose issue might be
prosperous, but would certainly not be expressed in the ordinary language of prosperity.
